It builds on the principles of differentiable rendering and Gaussian representation but diverges by removing the pose dependency [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method builds on differentiable rendering and Gaussian representation but removes pose dependency. The evidence explicitly identifies the method as 'NoPoSplat' (cited as [60] in S1 and [61] in S2). The evidence confirms that NoPoSplat 'addresses critical limitations by eliminating the need for known camera poses' (supporting 'removing the pose dependency'). Furthermore, the evidence describes NoPoSplat as using a 'canonical coordinate system' and 'intrinsics token embeddings' to decode into 'Gaussian parameters' (supporting 'Gaussian representation'). The context of the passage discusses 'novel view synthesis' and compares it to other methods like GS-LRM which 'tokenizes... camera parameters', implying the baseline involves differentiable rendering techniques common in this field. Since all specific factual assertions in the claim (Gaussian representation, removing pose dependency, specific mechanism of canonical system/intrinsics) are present in the evidence, the verdict is supported.
